title: Hoelder bounds pass to pointwise limits, and the limit is continuous
statement: Let n, l be natural numbers, L := L(R^n, R^l) with the operator norm, alpha > 0 and K >= 0 real, F_j : R^n -> L (j in N) and V : R^n -> L with F_j(z) -> V(z) for every z in R^n. Assume that for all z, z' in R^n, ||F_j(z) - F_j(z')|| <= K |z - z'|^alpha for all sufficiently large j. Then ||V(z) - V(z')|| <= K |z - z'|^alpha for all z, z' in R^n, and V is continuous.
lean_statement: ∀ (n ℓ : ℕ) (α K : ℝ) (F : ℕ → Rn n → (Rn n →L[ℝ] Rn ℓ)) (V : Rn n → (Rn n →L[ℝ] Rn ℓ)), 0 < α → 0 ≤ K → (∀ z, Tendsto (fun j => F j z) atTop (𝓝 (V z))) → (∀ z z' : Rn n, ∀ᶠ j in atTop, ‖F j z - F j z'‖ ≤ K * ‖z - z'‖ ^ α) → (∀ z z' : Rn n, ‖V z - V z'‖ ≤ K * ‖z - z'‖ ^ α) ∧ Continuous V
